definition: Slopaganda is a portmanteau of "slop" and "propaganda", referring to AI-generated content designed to manipulate beliefs, emotions, and political decision-making at scale.
details: The term is credited to Michał Klincewicz, an assistant professor in the Department of Computational Cognitive Science at Tilburg University, in 2025.

explainer.lead: Slopaganda is AI-generated content designed to manipulate beliefs, emotions and political decision-making at scale. It matters because generation at scale makes influence campaigns cheap.

tiers.eli5: It's machine-made junk content churned out by the truckload to change what people believe or how they feel.
tiers.practitioner: Analysts and platform trust-and-safety teams look for high-volume, low-quality generated text pushing emotional or political narratives. Detection is hard because volume and variation defeat simple filters.
tiers.paperLevel: The term is a portmanteau of "slop" and "propaganda"; it names AI-generated content aimed at manipulating beliefs, emotions and political decision-making at scale, and has no formal metric.

explainer.example: Thousands of AI-written posts repeating the same emotional talking point across social accounts would be described as slopaganda.
